      1. Overview and Acceptance

      These Terms govern 10key Survival, a game provided by Junhee Choi under the name House Duck in Germany (the “Operator”). They apply on every platform or store through which you play or obtained the game (for example itch.io, GamePix, Google Play, the Apple App Store or Steam; each a “platform”).

      You must accept these Terms to use the game. The shared House Duck Privacy Policy (section 13 covers 10key Survival) is a notice explaining how personal data is processed; acknowledging it is not blanket consent to that processing.

      These Terms are an agreement between you and the Operator about the game. Your use of the platform, your platform account, and any purchase, payment or ads on the platform are also governed by the platform’s own terms and privacy policy. If you obtained the game from a store, that store’s terms for apps, including its licence terms, also apply.

      2. The Service

      10key Survival is a single-player arcade game in which you steer a 3D numeric keypad over a board of keyboard keys. In these Terms, “the apps” are the Android and iOS apps, and “the web versions” are the versions played in a browser.

      Whether the game is offered on a particular platform, whether it is free or paid there, and which platform features (for example sign-in or ads) are available can differ between platforms. Today, for example, itch.io offers a free web demo of 10key Survival (up to level 8), and GamePix offers the full game free on the web with ads shown by GamePix, including rewarded ads that you choose to watch (section 6).

      The game includes:

      • Progress and saves: in the apps with a House Duck guest account (section 3), the Operator’s server keeps your progress (levels, upgrades and robot parts), scrap, gems, Rare Parts and modules with the account and decides every purchase and spend in the game; starting a run needs an internet connection. A run’s earnings count once the server has recorded the run; a run it cannot record (for example one sent more than 7 days after it started) earns nothing. In the web versions, and for players under 14 in the apps, progress and in-game items are saved only on your device or in your browser’s storage (section 3), and the apps can then be played offline. Your settings are always saved on your device.
      • Online rankings on the Operator’s server (section 7), which need an internet connection. Your results are sent with your House Duck guest account (section 3).
      • In-game items (purchases and further rules: section 5):
        • Scrap: in-game parts collected in runs and spent on upgrades.
        • Gems (gem keycaps): earned by playing and as free daily gems (for every 30 free daily gems you claim, you also get one gem set), on GamePix also by watching a rewarded ad, and in the apps also as quest rewards and by buying them in the store; spent on the one revive per run after the battery runs out, on Rare Parts and on the ROBOT PACK.
        • Rare Parts: obtained with gems and spent on module boxes.
        • Module boxes: a basic box opens with 1 Rare Part and a rare box with 3; gems cover any Rare Parts you are short of (1 Rare Part = 30 gems). Boxes are bought in the shop. You also get one free module box every day (it resets at 00:00 UTC) and one free rare module box for every 30 free boxes opened; the free daily box and the free rare box are collected in the shop. All boxes you hold, bought or free, are opened on the modules screen. A module box is a random item: its possible results and odds are shown in the game (modules > odds) and on the odds page before you open it, and a change to the odds is announced there and in the game before it takes effect.
        • Module draw tickets: in the apps, given as quest rewards and usable to open a module box.
        • Modules and module fragments, and the ROBOT PACK (section 5).
      • Quests (in the apps): daily and weekly quests. Your quest progress is counted on your device; with a guest account, a reward you claim is recorded on the Operator’s server so that it is granted only once (see section 13 of the Privacy Policy). Rewards are in-game items only (scrap, gems and module draw tickets).
      • In-app purchases (in the apps, optional): gem packs and the ROBOT PACK (section 5).

      3. Accounts and Platforms

      • itch.io and GamePix: the game uses a House Duck guest account only for the online rankings: you choose a nickname and the game signs in anonymously, without an email address or password. This guest account holds your nickname and your ranking results; your progress and in-game items are saved only in your browser’s storage.
      • Platform account: your platform account is provided by the platform under its own terms. The Operator cannot create, change, recover or delete it.
      • Guest account (apps): at the first start, the app asks you to agree to these Terms and the Privacy Policy and to choose a nickname, and creates a House Duck guest account for you, without an email address or password. The guest account holds your nickname, progress, in-game items, modules and in-app purchases. The app asks for your birth year and month once, at your first visit to the shop and before any purchase. Players under 14 play without an account: an account made before that answer is deleted (section 4).
      • Google or Apple link (optional): in the app’s profile you can link the guest account to a Google account or, on iOS, an Apple account, so that you can load the same account on another device or after logging out. Google or Apple provide that sign-in under their own terms.
      • Nickname: your nickname is shown publicly on the rankings. It must not be offensive or unlawful and must not impersonate the Operator or other people. The game refuses names on its word list, and the Operator may, after a proportionate assessment, refuse or reset a nickname that breaks this rule. You can change your nickname in the app’s profile.
      • Unlinked guest account: a guest account that is not linked to Google or Apple is kept only through its sign-in on your device and has no password or recovery code. If you log out, delete the app or its data, or move to another device, you cannot sign back into it, and the progress and items it holds can no longer be used. For a ROBOT PACK or gems you bought, see section 5. You can delete the guest account in the app’s profile (section 13).
      • Saves and resets: progress and in-game items saved only on your device or in your browser’s storage (section 2) may be lost if you delete the game or its data, clear your browser’s site data or play in a private window, and they are not carried over to another device or browser. The Operator holds no copy and cannot restore them. With a guest account, logging out or deleting the account resets the game on that device to a first start (your settings stay). This does not limit your statutory rights.

      4. Minors

      A minor’s contractual capacity and any need for approval by a parent or other legal representative are governed by applicable law. Where the law requires it, that approval must be obtained for accepting these Terms, using the game and making paid purchases. The platform’s own age rules also apply. Players below the age at which they may consent to data processing on their own should play only with the permission of a parent or guardian (see section 13 of the Privacy Policy).

      In the apps, players under 14 cannot keep a guest account or make in-app purchases: if the age question (section 3) gives an age under 14, the guest account is deleted, and they play on with their progress on the device only. This section does not impose additional liability on the representative or waive a minor’s statutory rights.

      5. Purchases and Refunds

      • Payment through the platform: where the game, or anything in it, is sold for a price, the purchase is made through the platform or store. It processes the payment, shows the price, taxes and payment terms, and its terms govern the purchase. The Operator receives no payment card data.
      • In-app purchases: the apps sell gem packs and the ROBOT PACK. The exact contents and price of each product are shown in the app and in the store before purchase. Gems are consumable: they are used up when spent (section 2). The ROBOT PACK is a permanent one-time purchase; after a run in which you reach the robot, it may be offered for 72 hours at a lower price, as a separate store product with the same content. Rare Parts are not sold directly for money, and module draw tickets are not sold.
      • Payment and verification: in-app purchases are paid only through Google Play Billing on Android and the App Store on iOS. The Operator’s server verifies each purchase with Google or Apple before the game grants it. A purchase needs a guest account and is bound to the guest account that made it.
      • Restore purchases: a ROBOT PACK bought in the store can be restored with Restore purchases in the game, using the same store account (Google account or Apple ID), also on a new device or for a new guest account. Gem packs are consumable store purchases; once granted, they are not restored by the store or by Restore purchases.
      • Lost gems: gems you buy are kept with your guest account on the Operator’s server. If you can no longer use that account (for example after logging out of an unlinked guest account, or after deleting the app or its data), they are not restored automatically. You can then contact support with the store order ID, and the Operator checks its purchase records.
      • Refunds: refunds and withdrawal follow the store’s or platform’s refund process (for in-app purchases, Google Play’s or Apple’s refund rules) and mandatory consumer law; for requests concerning the Operator’s own obligations, see section 10. A legitimate refund request or the exercise of mandatory consumer rights is not by itself grounds for a sanction.
      • After a refund: when a refund, cancellation or chargeback of an in-app purchase is confirmed, the Operator may revoke the ROBOT PACK bought with it. For a gem pack, the gems from that purchase are taken back from your gem balance; if some were already spent, the balance can go below zero, and gems cannot be spent until it is above zero again.
      • Purchase abuse: if objective evidence shows repeated purchase-and-refund cycles, receipts claimed for more than one account, or manipulation of purchases or of the gem balance, the Operator may, proportionately, refuse the affected purchases or exclude the player from the rankings. The player can contact support about the decision and request a review.
      • No cash value: in-game items and progress, including upgrades, scrap, gems, Rare Parts, module draw tickets, modules and module fragments, have no cash or real-world value and cannot be sold or exchanged for money. Gems, Rare Parts, module draw tickets, modules and the ROBOT PACK cannot be transferred to another account or player, and gems cannot be exchanged for scrap.
      • Game balance: to keep the game balanced, the Operator may adjust how in-game items (such as scrap, gems, Rare Parts, module draw tickets and modules) and upgrades are earned or used, subject to applicable law and section 11. A change to the odds of module boxes is announced in advance (section 2).
      • Nothing in this section limits your statutory rights (including your consumer rights) or the refund and restoration rights you have under law or store policy.

      6. Ads

      • Where 10key Survival is free on a platform, that platform may show ads (today on GamePix). It shows them under its own terms and privacy policy and manages any ad consent or ad choices.
      • GamePix: an ad may play when a run ends (never after your first run, and at most once every 3 minutes). Rewarded ads play only when you choose to watch one, and the game first says what you get, for example a revive, gems, or a sure success for a DRIFT or TRANSFORM card that otherwise succeeds at a fixed 20% in this version. If no ad is available, you get no reward and the game goes on. The game and its sound pause while an ad plays.
      • The Android and iOS apps show no ads.
      • The game itself contains no advertising or analytics SDK of its own; the GamePix version contains the GamePix SDK. Data processing for the game is described in section 13 of the Privacy Policy.

      7. Online Rankings

      • The boards publicly show the rank, nickname, score and level of players whose results are sent, to anyone who views them.
      • Results are checked automatically (plausibility checks and rate limits). A result that fails these checks is flagged and may not count for the boards.
      • The game shows the board of the current season and of the last season. A season is one calendar quarter and starts on January 1, April 1, July 1 and October 1 at 09:00 UTC (the current season runs from October 1 to December 31, 2026). The server also keeps each player’s all-time best for the player’s profile.
      • Season boards are deleted once the season is more than 12 weeks old. Other retention periods and deletion on request are described in section 13 of the Privacy Policy.

      8. Fair Play and Prohibited Conduct

      You must not:

      • Obtain scores or ranking positions by using cheats, bots, macros, other automation tools or modified clients, by tampering with the game, its saved data or the data it sends to the server, or by exploiting bugs or errors
      • Obtain scrap or other in-game items in ways that normal play does not produce. The scrap a player can earn from runs each day has an upper limit that normal play rarely reaches; the exact limit is not published, and earnings that do not match the runs played may be reviewed as possible abuse
      • Send data to the server other than through the unmodified game, or attack, overload or circumvent the server, its rate limits or its checks
      • Choose a nickname that breaks section 3
      • Manipulate purchases, receipts or the gem balance, or claim purchases made by others
      • Reverse engineer, copy or redistribute the game’s software, or reverse engineer the game, its code, assets, data or level design in order to make, or help make, another game built on the same or a confusingly similar concept or mechanics (for example a survival game in which a numeric keypad or its parts travel over a circuit-board world); in each case except as permitted by applicable law (see also section 9)
      • Violate applicable laws

      Where a violation is established, the Operator may, based on the facts and proportionately, remove or refuse records and exclude the player from the rankings, reset a nickname, take back in-game items obtained through the violation, or take the purchase measures in section 5. Where possible, the Operator gives reasons and an opportunity to request a review through support@houseduck.in. Exercising legal rights is not grounds for a sanction. These measures do not stop you from playing the game.

      9. Intellectual Property, Licence and Software Protection

      All rights in the code, graphics, 3D models, sound and music, level design, text, names and logos of 10key Survival, and in the game design as expressed in them, belong to the Operator or relevant third-party licensors. The Operator grants you only a non-transferable, non-exclusive licence to play the game on the platforms through which it is offered, for personal, non-commercial purposes, for as long as you comply with these Terms; all rights not expressly granted remain with the Operator. Where a store’s licence terms apply, they also apply (section 1).

      Except where mandatory law allows it (for example analysing the program to achieve interoperability), you must not:

      • decompile, disassemble or reverse engineer the game or any part of it, or extract its source code, assets, data files or configuration and balance values;
      • circumvent or disable technical protection measures such as encryption, integrity checks, anti-cheat or purchase verification;
      • modify the game, or create or distribute mods, modified clients, private servers, emulators or other derivative works based on it;
      • extract the game’s graphics, sounds, music, text or other assets to use them elsewhere or redistribute them;
      • collect data from the game, its servers or rankings by automated means (scraping, data mining) or access the servers through unofficial routes;
      • use the game, its assets or data to train, evaluate or generate output with artificial-intelligence or machine-learning models;
      • make, or help make, a game that is the same as or confusingly similar to it (a clone);
      • sell, rent or transfer accounts, in-game items or currencies, or use them in real-money trading.

      Gameplay videos and streams: you may record and stream gameplay and earn money from those videos. You must not distribute extracted assets separately or make your content look official, and the Operator may change this permission for the future.

      Feedback: the Operator may use, adapt and publish feedback, reports and ideas you send, without payment.

      If you breach this section, the Operator may, in addition to the measures in section 8, restrict your use and seek the remedies the law allows (such as injunctions and damages). Exceptions permitted by applicable law and your statutory rights remain unaffected.

      10. Statutory Conformity and Rights

      Statutory requirements for the conformity of digital products, the remedies arising from them and other mandatory rights remain unaffected. These protections take precedence also when locally saved progress is lost, records are removed, a player is excluded from the rankings, online features change or end, or the game balance changes.

      Where applicable, you may request remedies for defective digital products, including correction, a price reduction or termination, and necessary security updates. Store refund procedures are not the only route for exercising statutory rights; requests concerning the Operator’s responsibilities may be sent to support@houseduck.in. Statutory withdrawal rights do not automatically expire merely through downloading, use, or these Terms.

      11. Availability and Changes to the Service

      • The Operator may update 10key Survival. The online rankings depend on the Operator’s server and may be changed, interrupted or ended. In the apps with a guest account, starting a run also depends on that server; while it cannot be reached, no run can be started there. If online features end, 10key Survival remains playable without them for as long as it is available on your platform or installed on your device.
      • The online rankings are an additional feature. The Operator does not promise that they are always available or free of errors, that a particular result will be accepted, or any particular ranking position. Sections 10 and 12 remain unaffected.
      • Whether the game stays available on a platform also depends on that platform.
      • Changes or discontinuation for updates, maintenance, or technical reasons are subject to applicable law, including the requirements of German Civil Code Section 327r where applicable. Where required, this includes valid reasons, no additional cost, clear notice, information on a durable medium, and statutory termination or refund rights for impairment.

      12. Limitation of Liability

      Liability is unrestricted for intent, gross negligence, injury to life, body, or health, and any liability that cannot be limited by law. For ordinary negligence, liability for breach of essential contractual duties may be limited, to the extent permitted by law, to foreseeable damage typical for the contract. Otherwise liability is limited to the extent permitted by law.

      13. Termination and Your Data

      • You can stop using 10key Survival at any time. In the apps, you can delete your guest account in the game (your profile, then Hold to delete account under Account); on every platform you can ask by email for your data to be deleted.
      • Deleting the guest account removes its nickname, rankings, progress, in-game items (scrap, gems, Rare Parts, module draw tickets), modules, ROBOT PACK record and problem reports on the Operator’s server, and resets the game on the device to a first start. A ROBOT PACK bought in the store can be restored to a new guest account (section 5); other items and progress cannot. See section 13 of the Privacy Policy.
      • For serious or repeated violations of section 8, the Operator may exclude a player from the rankings permanently, after a proportionate assessment of the facts.
      • The right of both parties to terminate for good cause and all statutory rights remain unaffected.

      14. Changes to These Terms

      These Terms may be updated to reflect legal changes, changes on the platforms or service improvements. Material changes will be announced in advance on this page or in the game. Continued use alone is not automatic agreement to all changes or to optional personal-data processing. Changes requiring separate consent by law require that consent; rights under applicable law and mandatory consumer protections are not waived.

      15. Governing Law, Severability and Contact

      These Terms are governed by the laws of Germany (the Operator's place of residence). Mandatory consumer protection provisions of your country of residence remain unaffected where applicable.

      If any provision of these Terms is or becomes invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in effect; the statutory rules apply in place of the invalid provision.
